title: ReadFormatter incidents: the promotion defects and what caught each
desc: T3 dated archive for read-formatter-auto-elision: the two early returns that shipped in the first promotion, the deploy-order trap, and the measurements behind the budget. Core: read-formatter-auto-elision. Procedures: read-formatter-auto-elision-howto.
steps: INCIDENT: the first promotion shipped a SHALLOW substitute for the tested allocator and two early returns handed the input straight back. WHEN: a green build and a clean deploy still spill -- measured 2026-09-04, ElideByKeepTerms opened with a keep-term gate so a plain read never elided, and a second check counted bytes with its own formula. HOW: run wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring-howto, then grep the canonical file for the keep-term gate and for any second byte-counting expression before believing a promotion landed. WHY: the thin version built green, deployed clean and reported success at every gate, so nothing in the pipeline could distinguish it from the verified logic.

INCIDENT: dotnet build does NOT produce the staging binary, so a promote after it deploys the PREVIOUS build. WHEN: a source fix is committed and deployed yet the running behaviour is unchanged, with the output byte count identical across deploys. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wktest-staging-build-storm-safe-deploy-pipeline, then use bash bin/wktest-build.sh which builds the staging exe AND deploys it -- dotnet build alone only compiles the solution. WHY: measured 2026-09-04, three consecutive promote runs shipped the same stale staging exe and the payoff run returned a byte-identical 265.5KB each time, which is the tell that the executing image is not the compiled source.

MEASURED: a per-unit marker is unaffordable at scale and a shared footer is not. WHEN: deciding whether each elided unit should carry its own how-to-get-more note. HOW: run wkappbot skill read read-formatter-auto-elision for the tiered closing block, and put the retrieval sentence in ONE footer. WHY: at 200 units per-unit markers cost 13892 bytes against 10037 of content, 58 percent of the budget spent explaining what it hid; hoisting to one footer took markers to 702 bytes, 6.5 percent, and a footer costs the same at 20 units as at 200.

MEASURED: a synthetic fixture understated this feature by 64 percent. WHEN: sizing per-unit content from a test rather than from real data. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto and measure on realistic prose -- 16442 content bytes and 34.7 Korean characters per unit at 200 units. WHY: the fixture's words were 400 characters long so word-boundary truncation dominated, and a fixture that cannot occur in production measures the fixture.

INCIDENT: the seam compiled, deployed and printed NOTHING, and an unconditional probe was the only thing that settled it. WHEN: a read still spills after the engine is promoted, the build is green and the smoke passes. HOW: run wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring for the prove-by-evaluating rule, then put a probe at the seam that prints with NO condition -- an env-var-gated probe cannot distinguish a dead path from an unset variable in a child process -- rebuild with bash bin/wktest-build.sh, and run the STAGING exe by path. WHY: measured 2026-09-04. Probes at two separate seams printed nothing across five redeploys, and that silence was read first as dead wiring and then as proof the launcher must render skill read, which is false -- Program.MainRouting.cs only chooses Eye-pipe versus direct-core. The feature had been working the whole time; only the canonical wrapper was answering from a running core that still held the previous image. Five gates were green -- build, smoke, deploy, a 21 of 21 self-test and a commit -- and not one of them measured the command the user actually runs.

TODO: haiku-reflection reads 30523 bytes against a 30000 ceiling, a 523-byte overshoot meaning the reserve is under-counted. WHEN: picking up ReadFormatter work, or when a read lands slightly over budget while elision clearly fired. HOW: run wkappbot skill read read-formatter-auto-elision for the reserve contract, then check CalculateSkillReadReserve against EVERY line the command prints around the units -- the header block, the Steps banner, the Require and Expect blocks, the author and version lines, and each edit hint -- and confirm it walks the same collections the printer walks rather than indexing the first element. WHY: it does not spill, because the real transport boundary is 32768 and 30000 is the deliberate retreat from it, so the 523 bytes land in that headroom; but a budget quietly wrong by a fixed amount will cross the real limit the moment the wrapper grows a line, and the failure will then look like a regression in elision rather than in the reserve.

PROTO VALIDATION 2026-09-04: ReadFormatter-proto.cs (157 lines, no skill-specific nouns), SkillCommand-keepwire-v3-proto.cs (479 lines, equals canonical), ElideSkillSteps called but not defined (grep -c = 0). DefaultReadBudgetBytes constant has measured provenance with honest documentation. Four public static methods: ParseKeepArgument, ParseBudgetArgument, CalculateReservedBytes, FormatOutput. Ready for wiring step into v3 to replace inlined elision logic while preserving 479-line ceiling.

INCIDENT: the first promotion shipped a SHALLOW substitute for the tested allocator, and two early returns handed the input straight back. WHEN: promoting this engine, or reviewing why a green build and a clean deploy still spill -- measured 2026-09-04, ElideByKeepTerms opened with if keepTerms.Count == 0 return paragraphs, so a plain read never elided at all, and a second check counted bytes with its own formula instead of the shared helper. HOW: run wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring-howto for the promotion sequence, then verify the promoted BODY against the tested body rather than only that it compiles -- grep the canonical file for the keep-term gate and for a second byte-counting expression, and port the allocator out of .tmp/elision-test/ElisionTest.cs whose suite passes 21 of 21. WHY: a merge produced the thin version and it built green, deployed clean and reported success at every gate, so nothing in the pipeline could distinguish it from the verified logic -- and the size check is legitimate in principle, since output under the ceiling must stay byte-identical, so it stays but must measure through the same Bytes helper as everything else. The engine also exceeded the 400-line cap after the port and was split into ReadFormatter.cs plus ReadFormatter.Elision.cs, since fat-source-growth refuses any commit that grows a fat file.

INCIDENT: elision BROKE a live gate, because a shell script was parsing the output nobody thought of as an API. WHEN: before wiring this engine into any command, ask who reads that command besides a human or an AI -- and grep the repo for scripts that pipe it. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then for each caller search the tree for its name followed by a pipe or a command substitution; where one exists, that output is a MACHINE INTERFACE and truncating it is a breaking change. WHY: measured 2026-09-04, found only because the owner ran the tool by hand. wkwish calls handoff-wish-verdict.sh, which runs skill read claude-session-handoff-howto and greps for the literal string that begins the descent order. Elision truncated the step holding it, the grep matched nothing, and set -o pipefail turned that into exit 1 WITH NO OUTPUT AT ALL -- the descent gate died silently, which is the exact failure class this feature was built to remove, now caused by it. THE DEEPER FINDING: --keep did not rescue it either. Steering to the step still returns that step TRUNCATED, so a machine consumer that needs a whole unit has no path to it, and --budget only lowers. A full-retrieval route is therefore not a convenience, it is the missing half of the contract, and its absence is what turned a formatting change into a broken gate.

MEASURED: the transport spill threshold is BELOW the 30000 ceiling, so a read that honours its budget can still be lost -- bracketed 2026-09-05 to between 28416 and about 29900 bytes. WHEN: you are setting DefaultReadBudgetBytes, raising any ceiling, or explaining why an output that fitted its budget still came back as a saved-to-file preview. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then bracket it empirically rather than reasoning from the 32768 figure -- let a read of known size cross the tool boundary UNPIPED (a pipe to wc or tail measures the pipe, not the transport) and record whether it arrived inline; a spill is cheap to test because it returns only a 2KB preview, while an inline pass costs the full bytes, so walk DOWN from a known spill rather than up from a known pass. WHY: measured on bin/wktest-core-manual-v7.9.179.exe. skill read opus-self-reflection --budget 30000 produced 28416 bytes and arrived INLINE, while a separate session recorded skill read proto-to-live-wiring arriving at 29.9 KB and SPILLING. Both were under the 30000 ceiling, so the ceiling is set above the real boundary and the 2768-byte headroom this skill derived from 32768 is fiction -- 32768 is not where the loss happens. THE CONSEQUENCE: any read that legitimately lands between roughly 28.5 KB and 30 KB is inside its budget, passes every smoke assertion, and is still TOTALLY LOST to the reader, which is precisely the failure this engine exists to remove, now caused by the engine's own ceiling being too generous. The safe move is to lower the default ceiling beneath the measured pass point rather than to keep deriving it from a limit nobody has observed.
